resources.string: Got it
How to read it
Formula
More info about this metric
Headline metrics
Six top-line numbers for the selected range and mood filter: Sessions, Typing time, WPM, Error rate, Avg session, Longest streak. Each cell is computed from the same data hop and updates together.
Sessions, Typing time and Avg session move in lockstep with how often you used the keyboard. WPM and Error rate are quality numbers; Longest streak rewards consistency rather than volume.

Sessions = COUNT(sessions)
Typing time = SUM(ended_at − started_at) / 60000 min
WPM = keystrokes / 5 / typing_minutes
Error rate = 100 × Σ correction_weight / productive_keystrokes
Avg session = Σ duration / Σ sessions
Longest streak = longest run of buckets with ≥1 session
Time range

Picks the time window every chart and KPI on this screen aggregates over. Today uses hourly buckets within the current local day. Week is 7 daily buckets, Month is 30 daily buckets, All Time uses weekly buckets back to your earliest session.

Use Today to debug a single day; Week and Month for habits and trends; All Time for the long-running picture. Some charts (calendar heatmap, daily keypress bar, Usage Map) hide under Today because they degenerate on hourly data.
Mood filter

Restricts every aggregator on the screen to sessions you tagged with the matching mood. Tapping an active chip toggles back to All. The row is hidden until you record your first mood entry from the keyboard top bar.
Pick a mood to see how that mood\'s sessions compare. The Mood mix and Distribution panels stay unfiltered on purpose so a single chip never collapses them to one column.
WPM over time

Words per minute per bucket. Each bucket is one day under Week or Month, one hour under Today, and one ISO week under All Time. Autocorrect events are excluded from the keystroke count; emoji taps and backspaces are included.
A higher line means faster typing in that bucket. Gaps appear when a bucket has no captured sessions — they show as line breaks instead of fake zeros.
WPM = keystrokes / 5 / (bucket_typing_minutes)\nkeystrokes = COUNT(*) − COUNT(AUTOCORRECT)
Average IKD

Average inter-key delay in milliseconds — the time between consecutive key-up events in the bucket. The first event of every session is excluded (it carries the −1 sentinel since there is no previous key).
Lower is faster. Spikes usually mean pauses or thinking time mixed in. Bucket size varies with the selected range.
avgIkdMs = AVG(ikd_ms WHERE ikd_ms ≥ 0) per bucket
Error rate over time

Percentage of effort spent correcting per bucket. Numerator is the sum of correction weights (BACKSPACE = chars deleted; AUTOCORRECT = replaced span length). Denominator is productive keystrokes — events that produced kept text.
A bucket reading 10 % roughly means one in ten useful keystrokes was effectively reversed. Buckets with no productive keystrokes show as gaps rather than zero.
errorRate = 100 × Σ correction_weight / productive_keystrokes\nproductive_keystrokes = events − BACKSPACE − AUTOCORRECT
Gyro magnitude trend
Average device rotation speed (rad/s) per bucket while you were typing. SQLite averages the squared magnitude on the gyro samples; the loader takes the square root in Kotlin to get the line value.
Higher means more hand or device movement during typing. Hidden when no session in the range had gyro capture enabled.
gyroMag = √( AVG(x² + y² + z²) ) per bucket
Accel magnitude trend
Average linear acceleration magnitude (m/s²) per bucket while you were typing. Averaged in SQL as squared magnitude, square-rooted in Kotlin per row.
Higher usually means walking or otherwise unstable typing. Hidden when no session in the range had accel capture enabled.
accelMag = √( AVG(x² + y² + z²) ) per bucket
Calendar heatmap

One cell per day in the selected range, coloured by total keystrokes for that day. AUTOCORRECT events are excluded — only kept-text keystrokes count. Hidden under the Today range because a single cell tells you nothing.
Darker cells = busier days. Empty cells mean no captured activity on that day (or capture was off).
cell_value = COUNT(*) WHERE event_category != \'AUTOCORRECT\'
Daily keypress bar
Same per-day keystroke counts as the heatmap, plotted as a line over the selected range. Hidden under Today.
A jagged line means inconsistent activity day-to-day. Long flat sections are quiet stretches.
value = COUNT(*) WHERE event_category != \'AUTOCORRECT\'
Hourly distribution (24 h)
Total keystrokes by hour of day across every session in the selected range. Each row is one hour, 0–23, in your local time zone. AUTOCORRECT events excluded.
Tall bars are your high-typing hours; flat regions are downtime. Folding many days together makes the daily rhythm visible even on small samples.
value = COUNT(*) GROUP BY hour
Circadian heatmap
A 24 × 7 grid of total keystrokes by hour of day and day of week. Range-independent on purpose — always all-time data — because a single week or month is too sparse for a circadian pattern.
Bright rows are your typing windows; bright columns are your active weekdays. A bright column with dim neighbours points to a recurring routine.
cell = COUNT(*) GROUP BY weekday, hour (all-time)
Usage map
A bubble per active (day, hour) cell. Bubble area scales with the keystroke count for that cell. Hidden under Today since the X axis collapses to one date.
A solid horizontal band means a routine — same hour, many days. Vertical bands mean burst days. Tap a bubble to see its day, hour and count.
bubble = COUNT(*) per (day, hour)
Mood mix over time

Stacked bar per bucket showing how each Ekman category contributed to that bucket. Each segment is the percentage of mood entries in that bucket carrying that score. Bucket width matches the selected range.
A column dominated by one colour means one mood ran the bucket. Even splits mean a varied bucket. The chart stays unfiltered so a single chip never collapses it to one column.
segment_pct = 100 × count_of_mood / total_in_bucket
Mood distribution
Absolute count of mood entries per Ekman category over the selected range. Each row pairs the emoji with a horizontal bar scaled to that category\'s share of the total.
A long bar is a frequently-tapped mood. The bar width reflects share of total entries, not number of sessions.
row = COUNT(mood_entries) GROUP BY mood_score
IKD distribution

Histogram of inter-key delays. Buckets are log-scale: 10–20, 20–40, 40–80, … 5120–10240 ms. Anything above 10240 ms lands in the outlier annotation. Sub-10 ms rows are dropped (they\'re first-event sentinels).
A peak in the 80–320 ms range is typical natural typing. A second hump above 1280 ms is pause-driven typing. The "+ outliers" label counts very long inter-key gaps separately.
IKD = (key-up of N+1) − (key-up of N), excluding −1 sentinels
Dwell-time distribution
Histogram of how long each individual key was held down (key-down to key-up of the same key). Same log-scale buckets as the IKD chart. Outliers above 10240 ms are counted separately.
A tight peak around 40–80 ms is light, glancing taps. Longer tails mean lingering presses. Dwell is a per-key property and is independent of how fast you move between keys.
dwell = key-up timestamp − key-down timestamp (per key)
Flight-time distribution
Histogram of the gap between releasing one key and pressing the next (key-up of N to key-down of N+1). Same log-scale buckets and outlier handling as the IKD and dwell histograms.
Short flights are smooth typing. A heavy tail above 320 ms suggests visible pauses while moving fingers between keys.
flight = (key-down of N+1) − (key-up of N)
Orientation breakdown

Donut over sessions in the selected range, partitioned by device orientation at session start: Portrait, Landscape, or Unknown. Unknown covers sessions where orientation capture was disabled or pre-Phase-2 sessions that never wrote the column.
Each slice is sized by session count. The legend below the donut shows each slice\'s share of total typing time alongside its session count.
slice = COUNT(sessions) GROUP BY orientation
Avg session duration

Average length of a session per bucket, in minutes. Sessions still in flight (no ended_at) are counted as zero duration in the SUM but still bump sessionCount, so very short or in-progress sessions can pull the average down.
A higher line means longer typing bouts. Sudden dips often correspond to days with quick one-off sessions (a single message, an OTP code).
avg_minutes = SUM(duration_ms) / sessions / 60000
Sessions per period

Number of sessions in each bucket. Bucket width follows the range: hourly under Today, daily under Week and Month, weekly under All Time. Zero-bucket runs render as zero rather than line breaks since absence is meaningful here.
A flat line at zero is a stretch when the keyboard wasn\'t opened. Tall spikes are heavy days; this chart pairs naturally with the duration chart above.
value = COUNT(sessions) per bucket
Avg error rate

Per-bucket error rate. Numerator: sum of correction weights (BACKSPACE chars deleted + AUTOCORRECT replaced spans). Denominator on this Habits chart is the bucket\'s non-autocorrect keystroke count, including BACKSPACE.

Reads slightly differently from the Trends error chart and the global KPI. Trends and the KPI use productive keystrokes (excluding both BACKSPACE and AUTOCORRECT). Numbers here are usually a touch lower for the same data.
errorRate = 100 × Σ correction_weight / non_autocorrect_keystrokes
Avg flight time
Average flight time per bucket — the gap between releasing one key and pressing the next. The first event of every session is excluded (no previous key to measure from).
Lower values mean smoother sequencing between keys; spikes suggest pause-heavy sessions in that bucket.
avgFlightMs = AVG(flight_time_ms WHERE ≥ 0) per bucket
Activity quality scatter

One point per day in the selected range. X axis = backspaces that day, Y axis = autocorrections that day. The newest day is fully opaque; older days fade toward 20 % alpha so the most recent dot stands out.
A point near the origin is a "clear-mind day" — few corrections of either kind. Points far up are autocorrect-heavy; far right are backspace-heavy. Tap a point for the date and counts.
x = COUNT(BACKSPACE), y = COUNT(AUTOCORRECT) per day
Session metrics
Five headline numbers for this session: Events, Typing time, WPM, Error rate, and Mood (when tagged). Computed off one SQL round-trip via IkdSessionStatsLoader.

Events counts every captured key — including autocorrects. WPM and Error rate use the same formulas as the global KPI strip but scoped to this session. Mood appears only if you tagged this session from the keyboard.

Events = COUNT(*)
Typing time = ended_at − started_at
WPM = keystrokes / 5 / minutes
Error rate = 100 × Σ correction_weight / productive_keystrokes
Mood for this session
The Ekman category you tagged this session with from the keyboard top bar. Only the integer ordinal is stored — the emoji is rendered in the app from the score.
Visible only when you actually tapped a mood for this session. Clearing it requires re-tapping the privacy shield from the mood bar at the time of capture.
IKD over time (this session)
Average inter-key delay in milliseconds at every bucket within this session. Bucket width auto-scales: target 200 buckets across the session length, with a 50 ms floor.
Drift upward over the session length usually means fatigue or pauses creeping in; sustained low IKD is sustained focus. Gaps mark sub-buckets that were sentinel-only.
avgIkdMs = AVG(ikd_ms WHERE ≥ 0) per bucket\nbucket_width = max(50, ⌈duration / 200⌉) ms
Gyro magnitude (this session)

Average gyroscope rotation speed magnitude in this session, per bucket. SQL averages the squared magnitude; the loader takes √ in Kotlin per row. Hidden when no gyro samples were captured for this session.
Higher means more hand rotation while typing. Sudden spikes often coincide with re-grabbing the device or context-switching.
gyroMag = √( AVG(x² + y² + z²) ) per bucket
Accel magnitude (this session)
Average linear acceleration magnitude in this session, per bucket. Same √(AVG(x²+y²+z²)) formulation as the gyro chart. Hidden when no accel samples were captured.
Higher usually means walking or otherwise unstable typing during this session. Stable lines mean a stationary surface.
accelMag = √( AVG(x² + y² + z²) ) per bucket
